title: Where things are
verifiedBy: Claude Fable 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: The second case ending of the course, and the only one that never appears without a preposition in front of it — which is where its name, the prepositional, comes from. The everyday shape is -е on the end: стол → на столе, магазин → в магазине, работа → на работе, комната → в комнате, Москва → в Москве.

в is roughly "inside" and на roughly "on" or "at", but which one a place takes is as often a fact about the word as it is about the geometry: в магазине, but на работе — and nobody stands on top of their job. Learn each place WITH its preposition, the way you learn a noun with its gender.

есть means "there is" — it asserts that something exists somewhere: На столе есть книга. When you already know the thing exists and are only saying WHERE it is, есть drops out entirely: Книга на столе. That drop is the difference between announcing a book and locating one.

There is no dummy subject. English "there is a book on the table" has a "there" that means nothing and an "is" that agrees with the book; Russian has neither — на столе есть книга is simply "on table is book". Reaching for a Russian word to put where "there" was is the trap, and there is none.
здесь ("here") and там ("there") take no preposition and no ending, so they answer Где …? without touching the case system at all. They are the easiest answers on the rung.

Word order is already doing the work English gives to a and the. Книга на столе puts the known thing first and the news last: "THE book is on the table". На столе книга turns it round: "there is A book on the table". Both are correct and they are not interchangeable — M10 makes this the lesson.

words.note: "Where", asking about a position rather than a direction. Russian has a second word for "where to" (куда), which this level does not teach — M5's домой covered the only direction the course needs.

sentences.trap: Two words, and no verb — the zero copula from M1 has been quietly running under every sentence since. "Where IS the book" has an is that Russian simply does not write in the present.
sentences.sound: gdye KNEE-ga. Russian is comfortable starting a word with г and д together; say both, quickly.

variations.changed: swap what is being looked for — the frame is two words either way
a full verb after Где, and it takes the polite you-ending
a possessive word slips in front of the noun — мой agrees with what it describes

mistake.why: есть asserts that something exists; it does not fill the gap where English puts is. Где книга? is the question.

sentences.usage: Looking for something — the most-used question on this rung.
sentences.mnemonic: Where plus the thing. Russian charges nothing for the "is", here as everywhere in the present.

sentences.cue: The book is on the table

words.note: "On" — and also "at" for a place you think of as an activity rather than a container: на работе (at work), на почте (at the post office). It bends the word after it into the -е shape, exactly as в does.
Table. стол is the dictionary shape and the subject shape; столе is what в and на take. Masculine — it ends in a consonant — and the stress sits on the ending in both shapes: stol, sta-LYE.

sentences.trap: The answer to Где …? is where the ending appears, not the question. стол is the shape you look up; столе is the shape you stand things on.
sentences.sound: KNEE-ga na sta-LYE. The о of столе is unstressed and flattens to "a", and the е on the end softens the л.

mistake.why: на bends the word after it. Standing on something is на столе; на стол would be putting something onto it.

sentences.usage: Saying where a thing is — the plainest sentence this rung can make.
sentences.mnemonic: Look it up as стол, put things on it as столе.

sentences.cue: There is a book on the table

words.note: "There is" — the word that asserts something exists. It never changes for number or gender: на столе есть книга, на столе есть книги. It drops out completely when you are only saying WHERE a known thing is (Книга на столе), and it comes back in M8 to do possession — У меня есть книга, "at me is a book". One word, both jobs.

sentences.trap: The English sentence has four words of scaffolding — there, is, a — and Russian has none of them. есть is not "is": it is the assertion that something exists, and putting it into Книга на столе would change what that sentence claims.
sentences.sound: na sta-LYE yest' KNEE-ga. есть is one syllable ending soft; the ь is what softens the т.

mistake.why: The English "there" imported as там, which means an actual other place. Russian's existential sentence has no dummy subject at all.

sentences.usage: Announcing that something is available — the sentence a shop assistant answers a question with.
sentences.mnemonic: есть says a thing EXISTS. Where it is, is a different sentence.

sentences.cue: The bread is in the shop

words.note: Shop. Masculine, and it takes the same -е ending as стол: магазин → в магазине. This is M4's в again, doing its other job — the clock seat and the place seat are one word with two lives.

sentences.trap: M4 taught в for the clock — в семь часов — and it did not bend anything there. In front of a place it does. Same word, two jobs, and only one of them touches the ending.
sentences.sound: khlyep v ma-ga-ZEE-nye. The в here is barely a sound of its own; it leans onto the word after it.

variations.cue: The milk is in the shop
variations.changed: swap what is there — в магазине is unchanged

variations.cue: There is bread in the shop
variations.changed: reordered with есть — now it announces that bread is available
a verb instead of a bare noun — the place phrase is exactly the same

mistake.why: в bends the place after it, exactly as на does: в магазине. в магазин would be going into the shop, not being there.

sentences.usage: Saying where something is kept or sold.
sentences.mnemonic: M4's в told the time and left the word alone. M7's в names a place and bends it.

words.note: "Here". No preposition, no ending, nothing to build — it answers Где …? all by itself. Both ь letters in it are silent softeners.

sentences.trap: After a whole rung of endings, здесь is a relief and a warning: not every answer to Где …? is a bent noun. Some places are just words.
sentences.sound: KNEE-ga zdyes'. Another з and д together at the start, and the word ends soft.

variations.changed: swap the thing — здесь never changes
здесь → там: the other end of the same pair
reordered with есть — now it announces the book rather than locating it

mistake.why: здесь is already a place. Putting a preposition in front of it is like saying "in here-place".

sentences.usage: Handing something over, or pointing at where it is.
sentences.mnemonic: Some answers to "where" are nouns with endings. Others are just здесь and там.

words.note: "There", meaning an actual other place — never the empty English "there" of "there is a book". That job belongs to есть, and mixing the two is the module's main trap.

sentences.trap: English uses "there" for two completely different things: a place ("the shop is there") and a piece of scaffolding ("there is a shop"). там is only ever the first one.
sentences.sound: ma-ga-ZEEN tam. Note that магазин is back in its dictionary shape here — nothing is in front of it, so nothing bends it.

variations.changed: там → здесь, the other end of the pair

variations.cue: There is a shop over there
variations.changed: the same two words reordered — now the shop is the news

variations.cue: The key is there, on the table
variations.changed: там followed by the exact place, set off by a comma

mistake.why: One там is a place and the other is English scaffolding. Russian needs only the first: Там магазин.

sentences.mnemonic: там is a place you could walk to. English's other "there" is nowhere at all.

words.note: Room. Feminine, and it takes the SAME -е ending as the masculine стол and магазин — this is the one case where the ending does not care about gender, which makes it much the easiest of the six.

sentences.trap: M3's object ending cared about gender: only feminine -а nouns became -у. This one does not. комната → комнате and стол → столе are the same ending on different genders.
sentences.sound: AN-na v KOM-na-tye. The stress stays at the front of комната in both shapes.

variations.changed: swap who is there — the place phrase does not move

variations.cue: There is a table in the room
variations.changed: reordered with есть — and стол is back in its dictionary shape, being the thing that exists

variations.cue: Anna is not in the room
variations.changed: не in front of the place, since there is no verb to put it in front of

mistake.why: -у is M3's object ending, for the thing a verb acts on. Being somewhere takes -е: в комнате.

sentences.usage: Saying where a person is — and the sentence that shows this ending ignores gender.
sentences.mnemonic: One ending for all three genders. After M3, that is a gift.

words.note: Work, as a place and as a thing — the noun behind M3's работать. It takes на and not в, and there is no logic to recover: a Russian is ON their work the way an English speaker is AT it. Learn the preposition with the place.

sentences.trap: на normally means "on", and nobody stands on top of their job. This is the module's clearest case of the preposition being a fact about the word rather than about the world — and there are a dozen more like it.
sentences.sound: ee-VAN na ra-BO-tye. The unstressed а of работе flattens; the stress stays where it was in работа.

variations.changed: swap who — на работе is fixed
a pronoun subject, and still no verb in the sentence
не in front of the place phrase

mistake.why: Work takes на, not в. There is no rule behind it — it is a fact about this word, and it has to be learned with it.

sentences.usage: Where somebody is during the day — one of the ten most-said sentences in the language.
sentences.mnemonic: в магазине, but на работе. Learn the preposition with the place, not with the meaning.

sentences.cue: The key is on the table

words.note: Key. Masculine — it ends in a consonant sound — and it does not change here, because nothing is in front of it: only the word after a preposition bends.

sentences.trap: One noun bends and the other does not, in the same short sentence. столе bends because на is in front of it; Ключ does not, because nothing is in front of Ключ.
sentences.sound: klyuch na sta-LYE. The ч is always soft in Russian, closer to the ch of "cheese" than of "chore".

variations.changed: a place that needs no preposition and no ending at all

variations.cue: There is a key on the table
variations.changed: reordered — now the key is the news and the table is what we already knew
the question this sentence answers

mistake.why: The ending belongs to the word after the preposition, not to the subject. Ключ stays as it is.

sentences.usage: The most domestic sentence in the course — and the answer to the most domestic question.
sentences.mnemonic: Only what follows a preposition bends. Everything else stays as the dictionary has it.

words.note: "I live", from жить — pattern I, with ё in the you-form and the he/she-form: живёте, живёт. The жи at the front is always said "zhy" with a hard ж, whatever the spelling suggests.

sentences.trap: Москве is the third shape of a word M1 taught: Москва is the dictionary form, Москвы is what из takes, Москве is what в takes. All three live on one row, which is why tapping any of them opens the same note.
sentences.sound: ya zhy-VOO v mask-VYE. The и after ж is said as ы — Russian's ж is always hard, and it hardens the vowel behind it.

variations.changed: swap the place — and Индии is the same shape из took in M1, doing a second job
the polite you-form, with ё, after Где
the he/she form — живёт, ё still in place

mistake.why: в bends the place after it. Москва is the dictionary shape; living there is в Москве.

sentences.usage: The line that follows Я из … in every introduction — where you are from, and where you are now.
sentences.mnemonic: Москва, Москвы, Москве — one word, three jobs, one row.
